title: Relative restriction of scalars commutes with module stalk complexes
statement: Let X,Y be schemes [def-pc-scheme], f:X→Y a morphism, y∈X, and K an arbitrary cochain complex of O_X-modules. On X form the ringed space Z with ring sheaf f inverse image O_Y. Let k:O_Y,f(y)→O_Z,y be stalkPullbackHom followed by the stalk of sheafification. Let res be restriction of scalar sheaves along the actual canonical ring sheaf map tensorPullbackRingMap f [def-pc-module-pullback]. Then restriction along k of the module stalk complex [def-pc-module-stalk-functor] at y of res(K) is isomorphic as an O_Y,f(y)-module complex to restriction along the actual f.stalkMap y of the module stalk complex of K. No quasi-isomorphism, boundedness or K-flatness is assumed.

source.place: Tags 008H and 0098, inverse-image stalk germ formula; Modules Tag 01AG; specialization of the canonical ring sheaf map adjunction to schemes.

proof.text: Write alpha=tensorPullbackRingMap f and psi=alpha_y. Its defining adjunction gives unit followed by pushforward(alpha)=f.c. On a germ of a section over an open V in Y, the presheaf stalk pullback map followed by sheafification sends that germ to the germ of the unit section over f inverse image V. Applying psi and the adjunction equality gives the germ of f.c of that section, which is the defining germ formula for f.stalkMap y. Since every scalar is a germ, psi composed with k equals f.stalkMap y.

Scalar restriction leaves the underlying abelian presheaf and its maps unchanged. Represent a scalar in O_Z,y and a module element by germs, shrink to a common neighborhood, and use the germ formula for scalar multiplication. It identifies the action on the stalk of res(M) with the action on M_y restricted along psi. Further restriction along k and the preceding identity give the action restricted along f.stalkMap y. Thus the identity additive maps, in both directions, are linear and inverse.

The identity maps are natural for each module-sheaf morphism, since both sides use its unchanged underlying additive stalk map. Apply them to each term of K. Naturality for each differential verifies the chain-map identities, and the inverse identity maps give an isomorphism of complexes. This works degree by degree for unbounded complexes and for zero modules.

theorem relative_inverseImage_stalk_restriction_iso
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (y : X)
    (K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) ℤ) :
    let Z : RingedSpace.{u} :=
      { carrier := X.carrier
        presheaf := (TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageRing f.base Y.sheaf).obj
        IsSheaf := (TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageRing f.base Y.sheaf).property }
    let k := TopCat.Presheaf.stalkPullbackHom CommRingCat.{u} f.base Y.presheaf y ≫
      (TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat.{u} y).map
        (toSheafify (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
          ((TopCat.Presheaf.pullback CommRingCat.{u} f.base).obj Y.presheaf))
    letI := RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor_preservesZeroMorphisms Z y
    Nonempty ((((ModuleCat.restrictScalars k.hom).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
      (((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor Z y).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
      (((SheafOfModules.restrictScalars
        ((sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
          (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).map
            (Modules.tensorPullbackRingMap f))).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj K))) ≅
      (((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (f.stalkMap y).hom).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
        (((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace y).mapHomologicalComplex
          (.up ℤ)).obj K)))
